title: The Impact of AI on Productivity and Code (IEEE Software guest editors' introduction, Yedida, Menzies, Novielli, Jul/Aug 2026)

edges.target: Menzies retrospective on defect predictors (13/229 LLM papers use non-LLM baselines)
edges.ref: T. Menzies, "Retrospective: Data mining static code attributes to learn defect predictors," IEEE TSE, vol. 51, no. 3, pp. 858-863, 2025
edges.evidence: in a recent systematic review [80] of 229 SE papers using large language models (LLMs), only 13/229 ≈ 5% of those papers compared LLMs to other approaches.

edges.target: Kocaguneli et al., Distributed development considered harmful? (Microsoft auto-generated code)
edges.ref: E. Kocaguneli, T. Zimmermann, C. Bird, N. Nagappan, T. Menzies, "Distributed development considered harmful?" ICSE 2013, pp. 882-890
edges.evidence: it is known that Microsoft has been automatically generating its code, via traditional build systems, for decades.5

edges.target: Alshahwan et al., TestGen-LLM at Meta (11.5% classes improved, 73% acceptance, 75%/57%/25%)
edges.ref: N. Alshahwan et al., "Automated unit test improvement using large language models at Meta," FSE 2024, pp. 185-196
edges.evidence: the tool improved 11.5% of all classes to which it was applied, with 73% of its recommendations being accepted for production deployment by Meta software engineers.4

edges.target: Zheng et al., MultiCodeBench domain-specific results (GPT-4/3.5 below DeepSeek-Coder-33B)
edges.ref: D. Zheng, Y. Wang, E. Shi, H. Zhang, Z. Zheng, "How well do LLMs generate code for different application domains? Benchmark and evaluation," Proc. ACM, vol. 1, no. 1, pp. 1-22, 2024
edges.evidence: Research on MultiCodeBench reveals that all studied LLMs perform poorly on domain-specific tasks, with closed-source models like GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 showing relatively suboptimal performance

edges.target: Afrin, Xu, Mastropaolo, quantization of large code models (10% more security flaws; StarCoder 16.68 tons CO2)
edges.ref: S. Afrin, B. Xu, A. Mastropaolo, "Is quantization a deal-breaker? Empirical insights from large code models," ICSME 2025, pp. 1-13
edges.evidence: Training models like StarCoder (7 billion parameters) resulted in 16.68 tons of CO2 emissions, equivalent to four round-trip flights between Los Angeles and Rome.3

edges.target: Siddiq et al., code smells in transformer-based code generation (30% repository volume increase)
edges.ref: M. L. Siddiq, S. H. Majumder, M. R. Mim, S. Jajodia, J. C. S. Santos, "An empirical study of code smells in transformer-based code generation techniques," SCAM 2022, pp. 71-82
edges.evidence: Automated suggestions often introduce redundant logic and boilerplate, leading to a 30% increase in repository volume without a proportional gain in functionality.7
edges.section: Code Bloat and Technical Debt in LLM-Assisted Development

edges.target: Bisztray et al., LLM code stylometry (over 60% of model-generated C code has vulnerabilities)
edges.ref: T. Bisztray et al., "I know which LLM wrote your code last summer: LLM generated code stylometry for authorship attribution," AISec 2025, pp. 28-39
edges.evidence: Research indicates that over 60% of model-generated C code contains security vulnerabilities,8

edges.target: Roth, AI-generated code contains 2.74x more vulnerabilities than human code
edges.ref: S. Roth, "AI-generated code contains 2.74x more vulnerabilities than human code," svenroth.ai, accessed May 20, 2026
edges.evidence: Roth et al.9 identified a higher incidence of vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code compared to human-written code

edges.target: Asare, Nagappan, Asokan, Is GitHub's Copilot as bad as humans at introducing vulnerabilities (33.3% replicated, 25.5% mitigated)
edges.ref: O. Asare, M. Nagappan, N. Asokan, "Is GitHub's Copilot as bad as humans at introducing vulnerabilities in code?" Empirical Softw. Eng., vol. 28, art. 129, 2023
edges.evidence: Asare et al.10 found that GitHub Copilot replicated security vulnerabilities in 33.3% of cases, though it successfully mitigated 25.5% of them.

edges.target: Zhuo et al., BigCodeBench (60 LLMs, scores up to 60% vs human 97%)
edges.ref: T. Y. Zhuo et al., "BigCodeBench: Benchmarking code generation with diverse function calls and complex instructions," ICLR 2025
edges.evidence: models are not yet capable of following complex instructions to use function calls precisely, with scores up to 60%, significantly lower than human performance of 97%.11
edges.section: Complex Instruction Following and Long-Context Challenges

edges.target: Rando et al., LongCodeBench (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 29% to 3% from 32k to 256k tokens)
edges.ref: S. Rando et al., "LongCodeBench: Evaluating coding LLMs at 1M context windows," arXiv:2505.07897, 2024
edges.evidence: Claude 3.5 Sonnet's accuracy on LongSWE-Bench drops from 29% to 3% when context length increases from 32,000 to 256,000 tokens.12
edges.section: Complex Instruction Following and Long-Context Challenges

edges.target: Orel, Azizov, Nakov, CoDet-M4 (60,000 machine-generated articles; 97.56% detection accuracy)
edges.ref: D. Orel, D. Azizov, P. Nakov, "CoDet-M4: Detecting machine-generated code in multi-lingual, multi-generator and multi-domain settings," Findings of ACL 2024, pp. 10570-10593
edges.evidence: detection models can achieve up to 97.56% accuracy in identifying machine-generated code, with even simpler models like SVM and CatBoost performing considerably well.13

not_reuse_examples: [1] Muller/Torvalds: an opinion quote, not a measurement or method.
[14] He et al. LLM-as-judge: paradigm described as background; no number, result or definition adopted.
A1-A6 special-issue articles: summarized as the issue's contents, not reused.
Copilot adoption figures (1M developers, 20,000 orgs, 3B lines) are cited to [2] Zheng et al., an apparent miscitation; folded under the [2] MultiCodeBench edge rather than given a separate target.
notes: Editorial with no experiments: every edge is executed=false; v1's Menzies-retrospective sanitycheck is retyped numericfact (the rubric's own '5% compare to non-LLM baselines' example) and ten further quoted measurements added; TestGen-LLM edge is polarity=refutes because the paper says those numbers are 'unfair' without a baseline; the '[80]' inside the ref-6 quote is a dangling citation copied from the retrospective.
